raw_response:
I’m still doing wheat then maize on the same 2 mu, same as these past years. With only 2 people at home and some work outside, I cannot make things too complicated. Wheat-maize is steady for us. Wheat gives us the main grain, then maize comes right after, and if one side is not so good, the other can still help. I watch what the neighbors do. Most people around here still plant wheat in October and maize right after wheat harvest in June, so I will follow that. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless the weather is really dry.

For wheat, I will use the seed we know locally, not chase expensive new seed. I usually put a base fertilizer before sowing, then add some more when the wheat starts growing strongly in spring. I don’t dare cut fertilizer too much because if wheat turns yellow, yield drops fast. But I also won’t push too high because cash is tight. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is short, so I will keep tillage simple and plant quickly. I’ll use a local hybrid seed like most people do, give enough fertilizer for a decent stand, and water once or twice if rain is poor. I only spray pesticide if I really see weeds or insects. That saves money.
